summary: Adds the Garmin loopback SSO sign-in, the DI OAuth2 exchange and pre-call refresh, an identity assertion that refuses a token from the wrong account, and a one-time migration of the pre-press token file. Wired from internal/cli/root.go: registerNovelCommand runs configureGarminAuth, which replaces the generated auth setup/status/logout and hides set-token; registerClientHook runs installGarminFreshToken, which refreshes an about-to-expire token before the first API call for CLI commands and for internal/mcp/tools.go, which calls cli.ApplyClientHooks on the client it builds directly; addNovelCommandIfAbsent registers auth login, the generator's own novel-command scaffold with its RunE implemented in place as its header invites. No generated code was edited. REPRINT NOTE: the SKILL.md '## Auth Setup' block and the README '## Authentication' section are generated bearer-token boilerplate that a reprint restores; listing them in files[] does NOT preserve them (verified by control regen). Re-apply the auth-login choreography to SKILL.md and README.md by hand after every reprint until the upstream SKILL.md template honours the scheme's x-auth-instructions. SIGN-OUT CONFIRMATION ORDERING (N131.4h, finding F13): the H1 confirmation now fires AFTER the sign-in page opens, not between the logout and the sign-in navigation. Asked at the earlier point it can only confirm the logout page, which reads "Logged out!" whether or not Garmin then re-fills the sign-in form from a surviving SSO session -- and that autofilled form is the exact failure H1 exists to catch. The order is now: open the CAS logout, bind the loopback listener, open the sign-in URL (which already carries the state nonce in its service/redirect parameters), then prompt "Does the Garmin page show an EMPTY sign-in form? [y/N]:". Answering anything but y/yes aborts immediately with the sign-out instruction and never waits for a callback; y falls through to the existing wait. The prompt is skipped, and the previous advisory line printed instead, when nobody can answer or nothing was signed out: --no-logout, --no-input (which --agent sets), --yes, or no terminal on both ends. Two package-level seams in auth_login.go make this testable without a browser: garminOpenURL (production: openSetupURL) and garminIsInteractive (production: garminInteractive, which insists on a char-device stdin a test cannot supply).
reason: Garmin issues no personal API token, so the generated bearer-token contract (auth setup / auth set-token prose about pasting a key) describes a credential that does not exist. The spec declares a plain bearer scheme with no token_url, so the generator emitted no refreshAccessToken at all: without a hand-authored refresh the stored token dies after roughly 22 hours. The identity assertion exists because a browser that is already signed in to another household member's Garmin account silently returns that account's ticket, and nothing in the token itself names the account.
validated_outcome: go build ./..., go vet ./... and the auth test set pass. Both household homes were migrated off the pre-press token file and then proved live: auth status reports the right home rung, auth status --verify confirms the account with one call to Garmin, and the generated `account personal-information` command returns the matching userInfo.email through the generated HTTP client. The two homes report different account ids, and the legacy-config parse warning is gone from both. ORDERING (N131.4h): three new tests in garmin_auth_test.go assert the SEQUENCE rather than co-occurrence, by appending logout / signin / prompt to one slice from both seams. TestLoginAsksAboutTheFormOnlyAfterTheSignInPageIsOpen also GETs the callback URL parsed out of the sign-in URL at the moment that page opens and requires the 204 the ticket-less handler path returns, proving the listener was already bound, and asserts the 32-hex state nonce is already in that URL; answering N returns immediately with an error naming the logout route rather than waiting out a one-hour timeout. TestLoginWaitsForTheCallbackAfterTheFormIsConfirmedEmpty answers y, drives a synthetic ticket into the loopback listener and asserts exactly one exchange against an httptest token service reached through GARMIN_TOKEN_URL. TestLoginDoesNotPromptWithoutSomeoneToAnswer covers the no-TTY and --no-logout paths: no prompt, the advisory line printed, and the flow still waits. No browser was opened and no Garmin host was contacted.
